conventions.convention: Compression uses finite-dimensional CPTP encoders and decoders factoring through a code space of dimension M≥1, blocklength n≥1, and squared entanglement fidelity against an untouched purifying reference. Reliability means this fidelity tends to one.
Rates use natural logarithms: compression rate is ln(M)/n nats per source letter, and division by ln(2) gives qubits per source letter.
A cq channel has a fixed finite nonempty classical input alphabet and nonzero finite-dimensional quantum output; its n-use outputs are tensor products of the specified one-letter states.

Cq codes have deterministic encoder words, a uniform message in {1,…,M}, exactly M decoding POVM effects, average block error, and rate ln(M)/n. Capacity is the supremum of limiting lower rates over reliable sequences.
The gentle-measurement output is subnormalized: no normalization follows the operation ρ↦√Λρ√Λ.
Inverse square roots are defined on positive spectral support and extended by zero on the kernel.

Typical-projector surprisal sums omit zero eigenvalues. Conditional words need not give identically distributed eigenbasis measurements; acceptance bounds hold uniformly on a high-probability input set.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite-dimensional density operator ρ and δ>0, spectral projectors for ρ tensor n have mass tending to one, rank at most exp(n(S(ρ)+δ)), and compressed state at most exp(−n(S(ρ)−δ)) times the projector. For each finite cq ensemble and δ>0, a high-probability input set admits global and conditional spectral projectors with the stated uniform acceptance, exponential rank, and compressed-state bounds; conditional measurements need not be identically distributed.

For the finite ensemble and projectors satisfying the Statement's two acceptance bounds, conditional rank bound d, and global mean-state bound D⁻¹Π, independently sampled M codewords have square-root-measurement expected average error at most 2(u+2√u)+4(M−1)d/D.
For a finite-dimensional density operator ρ, 0≤Λ≤I, and u∈[0,1] with tr(Λρ)≥1−u, the trace norm of ρ−√Λρ√Λ is at most 2√u, without normalizing the output.
For nonnegative S,T on finite-dimensional H with S≤I, I−(S+T)⁻¹ᐟ²S(S+T)⁻¹ᐟ²≤2(I−S)+4T, with the inverse square root zero on the kernel.
If A,B are nonnegative endomorphisms of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and A≤B, then A¹ᐟ²≤B¹ᐟ².
For an (n,M) compression code, squared entanglement fidelity is at most the sum of the M largest eigenvalues of ρ tensor n, padded by zeros.
For each fixed finite dimension d, von Neumann entropy is continuous on density operators on C^d in operator norm.
For every R>S(ρ), compression codes exist with fidelity tending to one and limiting upper rate at most R. If a code sequence has limiting upper rate strictly below S(ρ), its fidelity tends to zero.

For a fixed finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel with the stated average-error convention, C_cq=max_p χ_p in nats/use. Every 0≤R<C_cq is achievable with rate tending to R, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most C_cq.

concerns.concern: F3 summarizes the cited bound as fidelity at most 'the sum of the M largest eigenvalues of ρ'. The supplier's Statement is about the eigenvalues of ρ tensor n. The proof correctly applies the n-block supplier in steps 1.2 and 3.1, but this fact summary omits the tensor power and is inaccurate when read literally.

Step 2.1 applies the packing lemma and calls the selected measurement a deterministic code. That lemma constructs (Λ₀,Λ₁,…,Λ_M), with an extra failure effect Λ₀, whereas the code Definition requires exactly M effects summing to I. The proof omits assigning Λ₀ to a message outcome; adding it to Λ₁ preserves completeness and cannot increase average error.

seams_checked.note: HSW F6 and step 2.2 use finite-dimensional SSA with a one-dimensional middle register to derive output subadditivity. The finite Holevo measurement supplier is also used with its exact finite-ensemble and finite-POVM hypotheses. No equality, recovery, or infinite-dimensional assertion is imported.

The typical-projector proof applies the finite-alphabet IID information AEP to positive spectral eigenvalues for the one-state construction. Conditional nonidentical words are handled separately by finite variance and Chebyshev estimates; no conditional IID conclusion is attributed to the AEP.

Checked the downstream uses of gentle measurement, fixed-dimensional entropy continuity, and HSW. Gentle measurement is used with unnormalized projected states, with scaling explained for subnormalized inputs. Entropy maximization uses continuity only in fixed dimensions. Weyl coding applies HSW to a fixed finite cq alphabet with finite output/reference space; the general EA proof fixes the block channel before taking its outer limit and explicitly avoids a general quantum-input single-letter HSW claim.
